reasons: Deviation classification is correct: a fifteen-day conformance window falls below even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services), and the express 'no correction or refund obligation thereafter' language undercuts the Section 19.4 remedy, so this is a material failure of the fallback rather than a mere shortfall from preferred wording.

The redline reaches the playbook position: period extended to ninety days, the cut-off sentence deleted, and the existing Section 19.4 remedy (re-performance, repair, replacement, refund) expressly preserved by cross-reference rather than duplicated — a proportionate rewrite of a single short clause.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact ('ninety days' spelled out rather than '90 days'); the 0.602 changed-character ratio is justified because the clause had to be rewritten to remove the obligation cut-off, and the rest of Section 19 (19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 19.5 carve-out) was correctly left untouched.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers a workable fallback (shorter period if it runs from acceptance and preserves the 19.4 remedy); the Section 6.1 acceptance-window point is a legitimate supporting argument.

Minor note for the drafter: adding conformance to 'the specifications in the applicable Order Form' goes slightly beyond the rule's documentation-conformance scope and beyond the minimum edit needed; it is a small, defensible improvement but could be dropped if the counterparty pushes back, and shifting the trigger from delivery to acceptance should be flagged as a negotiable point.
